_comment: Category-B (weak-copyleft) dependencies allowed by exception under P17 / ADR-0004. Each entry is a deliberate, isolated, reviewed allowance — NOT a place to silence Cat-X (GPL/AGPL/source-available). `package` is matched by exact name OR name-prefix (covers per-platform variants). gate:licenses fails on any Cat-B dep not listed here.

categoryB.reason: libvips native binary behind `sharp`. FINOS and ASF both classify LGPL as Category X, so this is NOT an allowed dependency — it is an OPTIONAL npm dependency that is never installed into any published artifact. It enters two ways: `next` declares `sharp` as an optionalDependency (clients/terminal), and `@huggingface/transformers`' IMAGE pipeline does the same (@vexa/mixed-pipeline). Both lanes omit it at install time.
categoryB.disposition: NOT SHIPPED. clients/terminal/Dockerfile installs with `npm ci --omit=dev --omit=optional`; core/meetings/services/bot/Dockerfile installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile=false --no-optional`. The Terminal never imports `next/image`, and the mixed lane is audio-only, so no code path loads it. Lockfile entries remain because the optional dependency is still declared upstream.
categoryB.scope: clients/terminal (next -> sharp), @vexa/mixed-pipeline (@huggingface/transformers -> sharp) — optional, omitted at install
categoryB.approved: ADR-0004 (revision pending: LGPL moves B -> X)

categoryB.reason: Native CSS transform/minification engine used by the Next/Tailwind toolchain. MPL applies to the unmodified dependency files, not to Vexa source or generated CSS.
categoryB.disposition: Logged exception; dependency remains an isolated build/runtime package managed by pnpm.
categoryB.scope: frontend build pipeline and Next CSS handling
